faq.q: Which years and slabs does this use?
faq.a: It calculates for FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27, noting that Budget 2026 left slab rates and the 87A rebate unchanged so the figures match. The New regime uses a ₹75,000 standard deduction with slabs rising from 0% up to ₹4L through to 30% above ₹24L. The Old regime applies a ₹50,000 standard deduction and slabs with a 0/5/20/30% structure, with the exempt limit varying by age group.

faq.q: How does the 87A rebate and marginal relief work in the New regime?
faq.a: If New-regime taxable income is ₹12L or below, the tool gives a rebate up to ₹60,000, usually wiping out the tax. Just above ₹12L it applies marginal relief so the tax can't exceed the income over ₹12L. For example ₹13L gross (₹12.25L taxable) shows ₹26,000 (₹25,000 plus 4% cess) rather than ₹66,300. The Old regime rebate is capped at ₹12,500 for taxable income up to ₹5L.

faq.q: Can the tool calculate my HRA exemption?
faq.a: Yes. Click 'Calculate HRA' and enter monthly basic salary, HRA received, rent paid, and whether you live in a metro. It takes the least of three amounts: actual HRA received, 50% (metro) or 40% (non-metro) of basic, and rent paid minus 10% of basic. The result auto-fills the HRA field, which only affects the Old regime. Deduction caps are enforced: 80C ₹1.5L, 80CCD(1B) ₹50K, 24(b) ₹2L.

faq.q: What's in the PDF and CSV exports?
faq.a: Both list your salary and other income, age group, every deduction claimed (flagging any that hit its statutory cap), and the tax under each regime with effective rate and annual/monthly in-hand. They state which regime is cheaper and by how much. The PDF is built in-browser with pdf-lib and uses 'Rs.' since the standard font can't encode the rupee sign. Everything is an estimate; surcharge/cess on very high incomes, capital gains, and business income aren't modelled.
